If it's there, I can steal it. The problem becomes how to present it. Presently I have a click going to the store page, but maybe that's not useful if you already own the game. I could change it to opening an overlapping div specific to that game.

Another problem is that the suggestions aren't necessarily linux games, and there's no way to tell without loading their specific pages. I'm not sure I want to get in to a situation where one server request is spawning 10 more proxy requests. I think while it might be neat to add everything and the kitchen sink, it might also be prudent to remember the ultimate goal.
Very true. Any thoughts on where you want the system to go? It seems to be useful and interesting as it stands.. But what are your future goals?

My goal was really self interest. I'm not actually a Linux gamer (I use Linux for work) but I wanted to see the current state of it in a way that was more tailored to my games. I figured if it was interesting to me, it might be interesting to others so my quick command line script instead turned in to a small webapp.

The project had two questions I wanted answered in relation to my own library:

  • Does my game collection contain Linux games, and if so, how many? (yes! roughly 30%)
  • Of those games, how many are ones that I've actually played? (the number goes up to about 32%, but the pool of games goes down significantly)

So really, the goal has already been achieved. Anything more at this point is tinkering because I can, not because it's furthering an agenda. I don't mind new functionality for the sake of it, but I don't want it to compromise existing features.

An Interesting piece of information that came out of the project that I wasn't expecting, is that many libraries (my friends libraries, mine, random ones I've scanned) contain a large number of games that never get played. In fact, in every single library I've scanned that contains 50 or more titles, less than 50% of games in a library even get run, and usually only a small percentage have significant durations of play.
That's pretty cool.. I liked the stats on playtime at the top as well. Universim is linux compatible btw.
